title: Slow Through the Mist
logline: High in the hills the fog comes down so thick that a train driver and a signalman can see only a few metres ahead. The only way through is to slow down and look.
human_question: When you cannot see where you are going, what does it take to keep moving safely?

premise.story: The railway workers of the highest stretch of the hill-country line on a fog-bound day: the signalman at a mountain station, the driver easing the train through cloud, the passengers pressed to the windows. Their work is to move through what cannot be seen without losing the way.
premise.place: A mountain railway station and the line around it: cloud forest, tunnels, a platform emerging from and vanishing into mist.
premise.experience: The fog of the whole group made literal and cinematic, then slowly thinned by patient, careful attention to one thing at a time.

concept_links.why: Delusion is the quality that darkens the mind so it cannot know a thing as it is [C008-M:L3]. The fog is an image of that darkening only; the film is about the workers' real practice of moving slowly and attentively.

The hindrances are described as a lid over the mind, and the helps listed include going out into the open air and recollecting light; the film can let that sit underneath the signal lamps and slow, careful work.

what_camera_could_observe: Fog rolling across the platform and swallowing the rails
The signalman's routines: tokens, bells, lamps, phones
The driver's view: a few metres of track, a horn, a speed kept low
The moment the cloud thins and the valley appears, if it does
what_must_be_real: The fog, the workers' procedures and the train's real journey. Nothing is slowed or repeated for the camera, and all filming follows railway safety rules.

possible_arc.opening: White. A bell rings somewhere in it.
possible_arc.turn: The train arrives out of the fog at walking pace.
possible_arc.ending_open: It leaves into the mist. Whether the cloud lifts or not, and whatever the workers really say about fog days, closes the group.

position_hint: closing candidate: the group's closing line made literal (the only way out of the fog is to stop and look closely), handing off to a group about slowing down and looking at a single moment

requirements: A high railway station with frequent fog and staff willing to be filmed
Permission from the railway authorities, including cab access if possible
Several fog days within the filming window

suggestions.name: Pattipola railway station
suggestions.why: The highest station on the hill-country main line, often in cloud.
suggestions.access_notes: Cab and signal-box access needs formal permission
suggestions.verify: Confirm current staffing, signalling practice and filming permissions.

suggestions.name: Ohiya railway station
suggestions.why: A neighbouring mountain station on the same stretch, with tunnels and cloud forest.

risks: Scenic railway footage becoming a travel film
Safety around moving trains and in poor visibility
The fog metaphor becoming too neat
drop_if: Railway permission for close filming cannot be obtained
